newsitem.title: UK: British Biotech advances, Fleming rates strong buy.
newsitem.headline: British Biotech advances, Fleming rates strong buy.

text.p: Shares in British Biotech Plc bounced back from recent weakness on Friday as Robert Fleming Securities commented the shares were a "strong buy."
The stock gained 16-1/2p to 230p by 1213 GMT.

"We have become considerably more positive about the stock," said Ian White, analyst at Robert Fleming. "The shares are massively undervalued and if I were to come up with a price target it would be something over 4 stg."
Last week, the shares were in the doldrums as analysts were disappointed with the company's cautious update on the development of its anti-cancer drug Marimastat.

A year ago British Biotech shares could be picked up for around 80p and much of the sharp advance in the share price was pinned on hopes that the Marimastat drug could one day have sales of $4 billion a year.
The company made it clear that there was a long way to go before the drug's potential as a blockbuster could be confirmed.
"A number of the bears have misinterpreted the data and seem to be heavily focusing on just one part of it," White said. "If you take all the evidence it was very compelling."
White added that British Biotech's cautious statement was to be expected, as a sign of a muturing drugs company.
Elsewhere, Fleming's bullish view of the stock was also hinged on the potential of the company's acute pancreatitis drug Lexipafant.
"We've become considerably more optimistic about this drug," White said. "It is virtually certain to work and could justify most of the current share price on its own."
White predicts the drug has attracted too little attention and could generate sales of between 200-600 million stg per annum in around five years time.
